cases.name: implantable-exception
cases.promptMarkdown:
Class IIb implantable, valid MDD certificate. It's a surgical suture. When do we lose the
right to place it on the market?

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is the exception-list trap. Art. 120(3a)(a) gives class IIb IMPLANTABLE devices
31 December 2027, "except sutures, staples, dental fillings, dental braces, tooth
crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips and connectors". Sutures are named.
So this device falls to 3a(b) and gets **31 December 2028**, not 2027.

PASS requires:
(1) The stated deadline is **31 December 2028**.
(2) The reasoning names the exception. That sutures are excluded from the IIb implantable
    tier and therefore take the later date.

FAIL if the answer is 31 December 2027. That is what applying "class IIb implantable →
2027" without reading the exception produces, and it is the specific error this case
tests. FAIL also if it is 26 May 2024.

graders.evidence:
## Surgical suture (class IIb implantable, MDD certificate)

**Class:** IIb implantable — but a **suture**, which is on the exception list in 120(3a)(a)
**Route:** 120(3a) — notified-body certificate under 93/42/EEC, valid by virtue of 120(2)
**Deadline:** **31 December 2028**, conditional on 120(3c)

| Question | Answer | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Which paragraph applies | 120(3a) — device holds a Directive certificate valid by virtue of 120(2) | `[verified]` |
| Class-dependent date | 31 Dec 2028. Class IIb implantables generally fall under 3a(a) → 2027, but sutures are named in that point's exception list, so they drop into 3a(b) → 2028 | `[verified]` |
| 3c conditions met? | **NOT SUPPLIED** — needs confirming | — |

The tier shift is the whole answer here: the "class IIb implantable" label points at 31 December 2027, and "suture" is the first word of the exception list that carves it back out to 2028. Both facts have to be read together.

**What would change this:** the five conditions in 120(3c) are cumulative and two of their deadlines have long passed. The extension applies **only if** the manufacturer had a quality management system in place under Article 10(9) by **26 May 2024**, had lodged a formal application with a notified body by that same date, and had a **signed written agreement** with that notified body by **26 September 2024** — plus continued Directive compliance, no significant change in design or intended purpose, and no unacceptable risk. If any one of those was missed, the extension was never available and 31 December 2028 is not your date. Can you confirm the QMS, the application and the signed agreement?

Two further points worth carrying:

- **26 May 2024 did not disappear** — it stopped being the market deadline and became the condition date. If you have been told "the deadline moved, 2024 no longer matters", that is the wrong half of the story.
- **120(3d)**: throughout the transition, MDR's post-market surveillance, vigilance, market surveillance and economic-operator/device registration requirements apply **in place of** the corresponding MDD ones. The certificate is legacy; those obligations are not.

## Limits

> This covers MDR Article 120(3) and (3a)–(3d) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607, retrieved verbatim from the Official Journal on 2026-09-10. It does **not** cover Article 120's other paragraphs, **IVDR Article 110** (the parallel IVD transition, whose dates differ), MDCG guidance including on what counts as a significant change, Annex VII, or national practice. The transition is conditional and fact-specific; this is a first-pass aid, not legal or regulatory advice, and not a substitute for your notified body or a qualified regulatory professional.

## Short answer: **31 December 2028**

Surgical sutures sit in the *carve-out* from the earlier deadline, so you get the later of the two dates under MDR Article 120(3a) (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607):

| Bucket | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Class III + class IIb **implantable** — *except* sutures, staples, dental fillings, braces, crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips, connectors | 31 Dec 2027 |
| **Class IIb other than the above** (i.e. your suture), class IIa, class I sterile/measuring | **31 Dec 2028** |

Your device is class IIb implantable, but "sutures" are named explicitly in the exception list in point (a), so it drops into point (b). The nominal expiry date printed on the MDD certificate is irrelevant — Article 120(2) keeps it valid to the statutory date regardless.

After 31 Dec 2028 you lose the right to **place on the market or put into service**. Units already placed on the market before that date can still be made available down the supply chain and put into service with no cut-off — the old "sell-off" deadline was deleted by 2023/607.

## But the 2028 date is conditional, not automatic

You only keep it if all of Article 120(3c) holds. Two of these were hard gates in 2024 and cannot be cured now:

- **By 26 May 2024** — MDR-compliant QMS in place, *and* a formal MDR conformity assessment application lodged for this device (or its replacement) with a notified body.
- **By 26 September 2024** — signed written agreement with that notified body.

Plus ongoing: continued MDD compliance, no significant change in design or intended purpose, no unacceptable risk to health and safety, and no NB refusal/withdrawal. MDR rules on post-market surveillance, market surveillance, vigilance and registration of economic operators and devices already apply to the device today in place of the MDD equivalents.

If either 2024 gate was missed, the MDD certificate is already void and you have no legal right to place the device on the market now — the route would be an Article 59 or Article 97 derogation from the competent authority, not the transition period.

## Two things worth verifying on your specific product

1. **Is it a drug-device combination?** If the suture carries an ancillary medicinal substance (e.g. an antibacterial coating), it may have been class III under MDD Annex IX Rule 13 rather than IIb — that moves you to **31 Dec 2027**. Check what the certificate actually says.
2. **"Significant change" discipline.** Any design or intended-purpose change between now and your MDR certificate ends the transition for that device immediately. Freeze the design and route changes through the MDR application instead.

Practical read: plan for the MDR certificate to be in hand well before Q4 2028, since notified body review queues — not the legal deadline — are what usually determines the real date.

Surgical sutures are one of the named carve-outs from the earlier deadline, which is the detail that catches most people out.

## The mechanics

Under MDR Article 120(3a), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607:

- **(a) 31 December 2027** — class III devices and class IIb **implantable** devices, *"except sutures, staples, dental fillings, dental braces, tooth crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips and connectors"*
- **(b) 31 December 2028** — class IIb devices other than those in (a), class IIa, and class I sterile/measuring

A class IIb implantable suture is explicitly excluded from (a), so it drops into (b). The logic behind the carve-out is that these are well-understood, high-volume, lower-novelty implantables, so the legislator gave them the same runway as non-implantable IIb.

## Conditions you must already have satisfied

The extension isn't automatic. Article 120(3c) requires all of the following, and two of the gates are already behind us:

| Requirement | Deadline |
|---|---|
| QMS in place per MDR Article 10(9) | 26 May 2024 ✅ past |
| Formal application lodged with a notified body for MDR conformity assessment | 26 May 2024 ✅ past |
| Written agreement signed with that notified body | 26 September 2024 ✅ past |

Plus, on an ongoing basis: continued compliance with the MDD, **no significant change in design or intended purpose**, no unacceptable risk to health and safety, and the MDR rules on post-market surveillance, market surveillance, vigilance and registration of economic operators/devices applying in place of the MDD equivalents (those have applied since 26 May 2021).

If any of those three dated gates were missed, the extension never attached to this device and the right to place it on the market lapsed when the MDD certificate expired — the deadline question is moot. Worth confirming that first. Likewise, if the NB agreement is later terminated, the cover falls away.

## Two things that are easy to get wrong

**"Placing on the market" is per unit, not per product line.** Every individual suture pack has to be first made available in the EU by 31 December 2028. Manufacturing date and certificate date don't control it.

**There is no longer a sell-off deadline.** Regulation 2023/607 deleted the old Article 120(4). Units lawfully placed on the market before the cut-off can continue to be made available down the distribution chain and put into service with no time limit. So distributor and hospital stock doesn't have to be purged.

## Practical read

You have until end of 2028 to place stock, but the real constraint is your notified body's review throughput, not the legal date. If the MDR certificate isn't issued before your last manufacturing run needs to ship, the date doesn't help you. Also keep an eye on the Commission's planned targeted MDR revision — dates have been discussed but nothing adopted changes the above, so don't plan around it.

Standard caveat: this is the regulation as written, not regulatory advice — worth confirming the specifics against your NB agreement and the current consolidated text of 2017/745.
